text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: page fired - INC-2026-12345 - inference-serving-high-latency. Trigger: 95th percentile latency > 1.2s for 5m. Affected route: /v1/generate (hosted-prod-us).

pagerduty: Notification sent to primary on-call (mike). Escalation policy: 3m -> secondary (jess) -> 5m -> manager (ops-manager).

mike: acked the page, looking now. seeing increased tail latency in prod. investigating logs.

jess: (auto-escalation note) will standby if primary misses ack. pinged infra-sre for quick lookup.

mike: root cause hypothesis: continuous batching timeout increased after last runtime deploy. CPU on node gpu-12 spiking.

anya: tagging customer-impact question: any known customers hitting errors? telemetry shows error rate steady, just latency spike.

eng-support: heard from one customer (acme-corp) reporting slow responses in chat flow, not 5xxs.

mike: running quick check: `kubectl top pods -n redwood-prod | grep inference` shows one pod at 98% CPU.

mike: attempting soft mitigation: curl health endpoint -> OK. trying `kubectl scale deployment inference-pool --replicas=6`.

sasha: heads up — autoscaler didn't spin up because maxReplicas was hit (6). we hit capacity cap.

jess: if primary doesn't clear in 3m, PD will escalate to me. mike, any ETA on scale?

mike: scaling command issued. logs show OOMKill on one worker earlier, might be noisy. waiting for new pods to pass readiness. ETA ~90s.

(2m later)

pagerduty: Escalation: primary did not acknowledge within configured window — paging secondary (jess).

jess: acked. jumping in. mike, can you paste the last 100 lines of the runtime logs?

mike: pasting snippet: ```
2026-03-14T11:08:12Z inference-runtime INFO batcher: batch_size=32 latency=1100ms
2026-03-14T11:08:13Z inference-runtime WARN kvcache: eviction_time=300ms
2026-03-14T11:08:13Z kernel INFO cuda: kernel_timeout
2026-03-14T11:08:14Z system ERROR OOMKill container_id=abcd1234
```

infra-sre: seeing GPU memory pressure across pool; one model shard pinned on gpu-12 causing spillover. Suggest rolling that pod and temporary scale up of node pool.

jess: plan: 1) roll affected pod 2) increase node pool by +2 GPU nodes 3) set temporary routing -> fallback model-small for non-SLAs. who can run nodepool scale?

ops-manager: I'm on call for manager escalation. If escalation policy fires to me, I'll approve burst capacity.

mike: rolling pod now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-shard-7 -n redwood-prod`

(30s)

mike: restarted shard-7, new pod coming up. readiness probes passing. latency still high but trending down.

pagerduty: Escalation: secondary did not acknowledge within window -> paging manager (ops-manager).

ops-manager: acked (manager). authorizing immediate nodepool burst +2 GPUs. tagging cloud-ops.

cloud-ops (infra-sre): scaling nodepool: `gcloud container clusters resize redwood-prod --node-pool=gpu-pool --num-nodes=12`

sasha: routing rule: setting canary to fallback-model (smaller) for non-enterprise customers to reduce pressure. patch: ```
PATCH /routes/cfg
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "fallback_model": "redwood-small-v1", "percent": 40 }
```

eng-support: notif sent to acme-corp that we're investigating and have temporary mitigation; asked for examples of slow calls.

mike: after roll and scale, p95 latency dropped from 1.3s -> 780ms over 4 minutes. errors remain low.

jess: good. set incident severity to sev-2 because user-facing latency impacting non-critical flows. opening incident ticket INC-2026-12345 in Jira and assigning IC to mike.

mike: IC confirmed. I'll run a controlled canary to fully restore traffic to primary model after monitoring for 10m.

anya: Customer impact summary for postmortem: "Spike in GPU memory pressure after recent runtime change caused a shard to OOM and reduced effective capacity. Result: elevated latencies for hosted generation endpoint, noticed by some customers; no increased 5xxs observed."

ops-manager: good summary. assign follow-ups: 1) quota/auto-scaler limit review (sasha) 2) runtime memory regression investigation (research + eng-runtime, jess) 3) improved PD escalation timing (ops-manager).

sasha: opened follow-up tasks in Jira: RD-847 (autoscaler limit), RD-848 (nodepool burst automation).

mike: handing off to next on-call (anya) in 20m. going to stay for the handoff notes.

(10m later)

mike: p95 stable ~640ms. traffic fully restored for enterprise via canary. continuing monitoring.

anya: acked handoff. taking IC if anything spikes before shift end. copying playbook steps to incident doc and adding timeline.

eng-support: reached out again to acme-corp; they confirmed improved latency in their flows.

ops-manager: since escalation policy hit manager, filing a short escalation blameless note: we should reduce wait windows from 3m->2m for critical routes. will propose in oncall-runbook PR.

pagerduty: incident acknowledged timeline noted: primary ack (mike) at 1780004335, secondary ack (jess) at 1780004402, manager ack (ops-manager) at 1780004470.

mike: closing actions before handoff: snapshot logs, attach kernel traces, add heap profile. then I am off.

jess: thanks team. nice quick triage. please add any missing details to the incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-12345

ops-manager: marking incident as "mitigated - monitoring". will schedule a blameless postmortem for tomorrow 10am PT.

eng-support: marking customer notifications as sent.

on-message: (reacted with :white_check_mark: by eng-support)

mike: leaving channel, handing over to anya.

anya: confirmed. I'll run the post-handoff checklist and update the doc.

(incident moved to status: mitigated at 1780004720)
